result: The authors report SCN1A expression detected by RNA-seq at D19 and D65, confirmed by qPCR at D19, D35, and D65, with no expression at D0. This is presented as evidence linking SCN1A expression timing to chromatin changes in the DS model.
evaluation: Reviewers note that RNA-seq and qPCR data 'do not on the surface appear to agree,' with RNA-seq showing 'little apparent difference between patients and controls' while qPCR shows 'a two-fold difference at D65.' This discrepancy is attributed to 'misleading artifact of normalizing PCR expression to that at D0 when the gene is not expressed but has mildly different low levels.' Additionally, 'no measurement of the protein product or its function is included,' which is identified as 'a major weakness that casts doubt on the core hypothesis that epigenetic changes play a key causal role in Dravet syndrome.'

result: The study reports accelerated chromatin changes in DS patient cells during early GABAergic development (D19), with DS iPSC showing predicted accelerated early GABAergic development that diverges from control patterns with continued differentiation, suggesting disrupted GABAergic maturation.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge 'an intriguing developmental defect in GABAergic neuron differentiation in this model' but express concern about 'how the absence of a sodium channel can accelerate differentiation when a priori I might expect the opposite (as less neuronal signal).' The correlation with SCN1A expression or protein abundance is not compelling, and the causal relationship between epigenetic changes and DS pathophysiology remains unclear due to the lack of protein-level validation.

result: The authors conclude that DS-iPSC have a disrupted developmental trajectory into GABAergic interneurons, shown by loss of motifs for DLX and LHX at D65, and enrichment of GABAergic-relevant TF motifs and pathways appearing prematurely at DS-NPC but not DS-GABA, suggesting perturbed GABAergic development associated with SCN1A variants.
evaluation: While reviewers acknowledge the study is 'novel and interesting' and shows 'an intriguing developmental defect,' they note that 'the correlation with gene expression or protein abundance is not compelling.' The lack of Nav1.1 protein measurement and the discrepancy in SCN1A expression data make it 'difficult to evaluate whether or not the observed epigenetic changes are causal,' which is central to the interpretation of disrupted developmental trajectory.

result: VPA treatment at D65 reshaped chromatin landscape to variable extents in different iPSC lines, with unspecific genome-wide changes that rescued dysfunctional development in some DS iPSC-GABA lines and predicted promoted GABAergic development in some lines, consistent with unpredictable clinical VPA effects.
evaluation: Reviewers note 'exploratory analysis that VPA alters chromatin accessibility at an individual-specific level' and that 'some of the variability in key results is better documented.' However, a critical concern is raised: 'Given that VPA would be administered in patients with fully mature inhibitory neurons, it is difficult to determine the biological relevance of these findings' conducted at D65 in an iPSC differentiation model. The variability is acknowledged but the clinical relevance remains questionable.

result: The differentiation protocol produces cells expressing appropriate stage-specific markers: pluripotent markers (NANOG, SOX2, OCT4) at D0, neural progenitor markers (FOXG1, PAX6) at D19, immature neuronal markers (DCX, NKX2.1) at D35, and GABAergic markers (GAD1, TUBB3) at D65.
evaluation: Reviewers note that 'representative images for cell-identity markers are now shown for D19 and D65' as a weakness that was addressed. This indicates the reviewers accepted the marker expression data as supporting the differentiation protocol, though they initially requested better documentation.

result: ATAC-Seq captured 58,382-74,561 accessible chromatin peaks at different time points, with PCA showing biological replicates separating into four clusters corresponding to differentiation stages, and genome-wide correlation with RNA-Seq of 0.52-0.57 indicating good data quality.
evaluation: Reviewers note that 'some features of ATAC signal normalization and enrichment analysis have been better documented' and 'some QC on ATAC is described,' indicating acceptance of the technical quality of ATAC-Seq data. The correlation values and clustering are presented as quality control metrics that reviewers did not challenge.

result: Control iPSC during GABAergic differentiation show 19,931 differential peaks clustering into four distinct patterns (Ctl-iPSC, Ctl-NPC, Ctl-imN, Ctl-GABA) with stage-specific genomic distributions, TF motif enrichments (pluripotency TFs at D0, SOX family at D19, LHX/NKX/DLX at later stages), and pathway enrichments consistent with in vivo GABAergic development.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the study is 'well written with good graphics and flow' and that technical aspects of ATAC analysis have been 'better documented.' The control differentiation data serves as the baseline for comparison and was not specifically challenged, suggesting implicit acceptance of these characterization results.

result: The authors acknowledge that the iPSC model has limitations: the 65-day directed differentiation protocol may not fully recapitulate in vivo GABAergic maturation, and iPSC differentiation models typically do not reach cellular states comparable to postnatal cell types where functional maturation occurs.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly note this limitation, stating 'Given that VPA would be administered in patients with fully mature inhibitory neurons, it is difficult to determine the biological relevance of these findings.' This indicates reviewers agree with the authors' acknowledgment of model limitations, though they emphasize this as a significant concern for interpretation.

result: One DS-iPSC line (DD4A) did not differentiate up to D65 for unknown reasons, so D65 data are based on two DS-iPSC lines.
evaluation: Reviewers note concerns about variability and that 'the authors describe a method for trying to diminish variability but do not adequately explain this method or how much variability remains in many of their measures.' The loss of one cell line at D65 contributes to this variability concern but is acknowledged as a technical limitation rather than disputed.

result: Immunostaining revealed comparable number and morphology of DS-patient and control GABAergic neurons, similar to Scn1a+/- mouse models showing intact interneuron density despite impaired function, suggesting relatively preserved proliferative capacity during GABAergic development in DS.
evaluation: Reviewers note that 'the authors address a possible role for cell death in data obtained from their cultures by assessing viability with trypan blue staining' as a weakness that was addressed. This indicates acceptance of the cell viability and morphology data, though it was initially a concern requiring additional evidence.
